data.targetWord: A large stone or decorative basin near the church entrance used for baptism, symbolising entry into the Christian community

examples.en-GB: The priest baptised the infant at the font near the church door.

data.targetWord: The central table in a church used for Holy Communion (Eucharist), representing Christ's sacrifice

examples.en-GB: The congregation gathered around the altar to receive communion.

data.targetWord: An elevated platform in a church from which the sermon (religious teaching) is delivered

examples.en-GB: The minister stood in the pulpit to deliver the Sunday sermon.

data.targetWord: The main central hall of a church where the congregation sits during worship

examples.en-GB: Rows of wooden pews filled the nave of the old cathedral.

data.targetWord: A niche or alcove in the wall of a mosque that indicates the direction of Mecca (qibla), towards which Muslims pray

examples.en-GB: The imam stood near the mihrab to lead Friday prayers.

data.targetWord: A raised pulpit or platform in a mosque from which the imam delivers the Friday sermon (khutbah)

examples.en-GB: The imam climbed the steps of the minbar to address the congregation.

data.targetWord: The Islamic ritual washing of hands, face, and feet performed before prayer as an act of purification

examples.en-GB: Worshippers perform wudu at the ablution fountains before entering the prayer hall.

data.targetWord: A tall tower attached to a mosque from which the adhan (call to prayer) is traditionally announced

examples.en-GB: The muezzin's call to prayer rang out from the minaret at dawn.

data.targetWord: The Holy Ark — an ornamental cabinet in the synagogue that houses the Torah scrolls, positioned on the wall facing Jerusalem

examples.en-GB: The congregation rose when the doors of the Aron HaKodesh were opened.

data.targetWord: The Eternal Light — a lamp that burns continuously above the Aron HaKodesh in a synagogue, symbolising God's eternal presence

examples.en-GB: The Ner Tamid is never extinguished, representing God's constant presence.

data.targetWord: A raised platform in the centre (or front) of a synagogue from which the Torah is read aloud during services

examples.en-GB: The rabbi read from the Torah scroll on the bimah.

data.targetWord: A sacred image or statue of a Hindu deity, treated as a physical form of the divine and used as a focus for worship (puja)

examples.en-GB: The murti of Ganesha was decorated with flowers and offered food as part of the morning puja.

data.targetWord: Hindu worship involving offerings, prayers, and rituals directed towards a murti (deity image), performed at home or in a mandir

examples.en-GB: The family gathered at the home shrine to perform morning puja.

data.targetWord: Blessed food offered to a deity during Hindu puja and then distributed to worshippers as a gift from the divine

examples.en-GB: After the aarti ceremony, prasad was shared among all who attended the mandir.

data.targetWord: The Sikh flag — a triangular saffron-coloured banner bearing the Khanda symbol, flown outside every gurdwara to identify it as a Sikh place of worship

examples.en-GB: The Nishan Sahib flying outside the building showed it was a gurdwara.

data.targetWord: A raised throne or platform in the gurdwara's prayer hall on which the Guru Granth Sahib rests, treated with the respect due to a living Guru

examples.en-GB: The Guru Granth Sahib is placed on the takht and covered with a decorative cloth when not in use.

data.targetWord: The community kitchen and free meal served in every gurdwara to all visitors regardless of faith, background, or status, expressing equality and seva

examples.en-GB: After the service, everyone was welcome to eat together in the langar hall.

data.targetWord: The devotional singing of hymns (shabads) from the Guru Granth Sahib, central to Sikh worship in the gurdwara

examples.en-GB: The raagi musicians led the congregation in kirtan throughout the morning service.

data.targetWord: A dome-shaped Buddhist monument or shrine, originally built to house relics of the Buddha, now used as a focus for meditation and devotion

examples.en-GB: Buddhists walk clockwise around the stupa as an act of veneration.

data.targetWord: A sacred space or altar containing a Buddha image and offerings (flowers, candles, incense), used as a focal point for meditation and reflection

examples.en-GB: Worshippers placed flowers at the shrine as an act of respect and mindfulness.

data.targetWord: A dedicated sacred space within a family home used for daily personal worship, prayer, or meditation — found in many religious traditions

examples.en-GB: Many Hindu families maintain a home shrine where they perform puja each morning.

data.targetWord: The community of worshippers who gather together for religious services or prayer at a place of worship

examples.en-GB: The congregation sang hymns together during Sunday morning worship.

data.targetWord: The Islamic concept of the absolute oneness of God — the reason mosques contain no images of God, prophets, or humans

examples.en-GB: Because of tawhid, mosque decoration uses geometric patterns and calligraphy rather than images.

data.targetWord: A handwritten parchment scroll containing the first five books of the Hebrew Bible, kept in the Aron HaKodesh and read aloud in synagogue services

examples.en-GB: The Torah scroll is dressed in a velvet cover and carried through the synagogue with great reverence.

data.targetWord: A reading stand in a church from which the Bible is read aloud during services, often shaped like an eagle symbolising the spread of the Gospel

examples.en-GB: The reader stood at the lectern to read the Epistle to the congregation.

data.title: Put these steps of a Muslim's visit to the mosque for Friday prayer in the correct order.
items: Hear the adhan (call to prayer) from the minaret
Perform wudu (ritual washing) in the ablution area
Remove shoes and enter the prayer hall
Face the mihrab and pray in rows behind the imam
Listen to the khutbah (sermon) delivered from the minbar

data.title: Put these elements of a synagogue Shabbat service in the correct order.
items: The congregation rises as the Aron HaKodesh is opened
The Torah scroll is carried to the bimah
The Torah portion is read aloud in Hebrew
The scroll is returned to the Aron HaKodesh
The rabbi delivers a sermon (drash) on the reading

data.title: Put these actions in the correct order for a typical Hindu puja ceremony at a mandir.
items: Ring the bell on entering to alert the deity to the worshipper's presence
Present offerings of flowers, food, and water to the murti
Wave the aarti lamp before the deity as a symbol of devotion
Receive prasad (blessed food) from the priest
Bow in namaste as a gesture of respect before leaving
